apis.name: RegOpenKeyExW
apis.summary: Opens an existing registry key with the requested access rights.
apis.description: RegOpenKeyExW opens the key named by lpSubKey relative to an open or predefined root key. The samDesired mask determines whether the returned handle can query values, enumerate subkeys, set values, or create subkeys. The function does not create the key; use RegCreateKeyExW when the key may not exist.
apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegOpenKeyExW(HKEY hKey, LPCWSTR lpSubKey, DWORD ulOptions, REGSAM samDesired, PHKEY phkResult);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open key or one of the predefined root keys, such as HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE or HKEY_CURRENT_USER. The key is the starting point for the relative subkey path.

parameters.name: lpSubKey
parameters.description: The name of the subkey to open, relative to hKey. Key names are not case sensitive, and a path may contain multiple levels.

parameters.name: ulOptions
parameters.description: Reserved. It must be zero.

parameters.name: samDesired
parameters.description: The access mask for the returned handle, such as KEY_READ to query values and enumerate subkeys, KEY_WRITE to set values, or KEY_ALL_ACCESS. Request only the rights the task needs.

parameters.name: phkResult
parameters.description: Receives a handle to the opened key. Close it with RegCloseKey when it is no longer needed.

return.success: ERROR_SUCCESS (zero). phkResult contains a valid key handle.
return.failure: A nonzero Win32 error code, returned directly. Common values include ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND and ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. Do not call GetLastError to diagnose this function.

apis.unicode_notes: RegOpenKeyExW is the Unicode variant. RegOpenKeyExA accepts an ANSI subkey name, and the encoding-neutral RegOpenKeyEx alias resolves to one of them at compile time.
apis.remarks: Registry functions report failures through their LSTATUS return value rather than GetLastError. Handles returned by this function must be closed with RegCloseKey. On 64-bit Windows, a 32-bit process may see a redirected view of certain keys unless a WOW64 access flag is included in samDesired.
apis.maldev_notes: Reading registry configuration is routine in installers, licensing code, and software that discovers installed components or system settings. Analysts usually consider the key path, the requested access, and the number of queries rather than the open call alone.
apis.defensive_notes: Registry access telemetry, where collected, typically records the key path and requested access. Broad or repeated access to sensitive keys by a process whose role does not explain it can merit review, but reads are extremely common.
apis.source_notes: Prototype, LSTATUS error convention, and access-mask semantics checked against Microsoft Learn (winreg.h).

apis.name: RegCreateKeyExW
apis.summary: Creates a registry key or opens it if it already exists.
apis.description: RegCreateKeyExW creates the key named by lpSubKey under hKey and, as documented, creates any missing intermediate keys in the path. If the key already exists, the function opens it instead. The disposition output distinguishes a newly created key from an existing one, and the returned handle can be used to set values.
apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegCreateKeyExW(HKEY hKey, LPCWSTR lpSubKey, DWORD Reserved, LPWSTR lpClass, DWORD dwOptions, REGSAM samDesired, const LPSECURITY_ATTRIBUTES lpSecurityAttributes, PHKEY phkResult, LPDWORD lpdwDisposition);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open key or a predefined root key under which the subkey is created. Creating a direct child of HKEY_USERS or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE is not supported; create keys at lower levels instead.

parameters.name: lpSubKey
parameters.description: The name of the subkey to create or open, relative to hKey. The path can be up to 32 levels deep. An empty string causes phkResult to receive a new handle to hKey. The parameter cannot be NULL.

parameters.name: Reserved
parameters.description: Reserved. It must be zero.

parameters.name: lpClass
parameters.description: An optional user-defined class string for the key. The parameter may be ignored and can be NULL.

parameters.name: dwOptions
parameters.description: Key options: REG_OPTION_NON_VOLATILE (the default, stored in the hive file), REG_OPTION_VOLATILE, REG_OPTION_BACKUP_RESTORE, or REG_OPTION_CREATE_LINK.

parameters.name: samDesired
parameters.description: The access mask for the returned handle, such as KEY_WRITE or KEY_ALL_ACCESS, optionally combined with a WOW64 view flag.

parameters.name: lpSecurityAttributes
parameters.description: An optional SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES structure that determines whether the handle can be inherited and supplies a security descriptor for the new key. NULL gives a default descriptor and a non-inheritable handle.

parameters.name: phkResult
parameters.description: Receives a handle to the created or opened key. Close it with RegCloseKey.

parameters.name: lpdwDisposition
parameters.description: An optional pointer that receives REG_CREATED_NEW_KEY or REG_OPENED_EXISTING_KEY. NULL suppresses disposition information.

return.success: ERROR_SUCCESS (zero). phkResult contains a valid key handle.
return.failure: A nonzero Win32 error code, returned directly. Do not call GetLastError to diagnose this function.

apis.unicode_notes: RegCreateKeyExW is the Unicode variant. RegCreateKeyExA accepts an ANSI subkey name, and the encoding-neutral RegCreateKeyEx alias resolves to one of them at compile time.
apis.remarks: The function creates all missing keys in the specified path, so a misspelled path can create unwanted keys. A newly created key has no values; use RegSetValueExW to write them. Close the returned handle with RegCloseKey.
apis.maldev_notes: Key creation appears in installers, per-user configuration, and many other ordinary scenarios. Analysts tend to focus on the key path and the values written afterward, since creation by itself is not a meaningful indicator.
apis.defensive_notes: Registry key-creation telemetry can be correlated with value-set events to reconstruct which configuration a process wrote. The writing process, key path, and subsequent value data are the most useful fields.
apis.source_notes: Prototype, intermediate-key creation behavior, and disposition values checked against Microsoft Learn (winreg.h).

apis.name: RegQueryValueExW
apis.summary: Retrieves the type and data of a named registry value.
apis.description: RegQueryValueExW reads the data and type of a value under an open key. Callers commonly invoke it twice: first with a NULL data buffer to learn the required size and the type, then again with an allocated buffer. If the buffer is too small, the function returns ERROR_MORE_DATA and reports the required size.
apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegQueryValueExW(HKEY hKey, LPCWSTR lpValueName, LPDWORD lpReserved, LPDWORD lpType, LPBYTE lpData, LPDWORD lpcbData);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open key with query access, typically KEY_QUERY_VALUE or KEY_READ. It may also be a predefined root key.

parameters.name: lpValueName
parameters.description: The name of the value to query. A NULL pointer or an empty string addresses the key's default (unnamed) value, if one exists.

parameters.name: lpReserved
parameters.description: Reserved. It must be NULL.

parameters.name: lpType
parameters.description: An optional pointer that receives the value's type code, such as REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, or REG_DWORD.

parameters.name: lpData
parameters.description: An optional buffer that receives the value data. NULL requests only the required size and type. The buffer is interpreted according to the returned type.

parameters.name: lpcbData
parameters.description: On input, the size of lpData in bytes. On success, receives the number of bytes copied. If the buffer is too small, receives the required size and the function returns ERROR_MORE_DATA.

return.success: ERROR_SUCCESS (zero). lpType and lpData describe the value, and lpcbData reports the bytes copied.
return.failure: A nonzero Win32 error code, returned directly. ERROR_MORE_DATA means the buffer was too small; ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND means the value does not exist.

apis.unicode_notes: RegQueryValueExW is the Unicode variant and returns REG_SZ data as UTF-16LE code units. RegQueryValueExA is the ANSI variant, and the encoding-neutral RegQueryValueEx alias resolves at compile time.
apis.remarks: lpcbData is a byte count, not a character count. When querying string data, leave room for the terminating null character and validate both the returned type and size before treating the buffer as a string. The required size can change between the sizing call and the read.
apis.maldev_notes: Configuration, version, and licensing data are commonly read from the registry. Analysts may inspect which values a program consults, but registry reads are extremely common and only meaningful in context.
apis.defensive_notes: Registry query telemetry can be high volume. Repeated queries around security settings or auto-start configuration can be interesting, but should be evaluated against the process's role and normal behavior.

apis.name: RegSetValueExW
apis.summary: Sets the type and data of a named registry value under an open key.
apis.description: RegSetValueExW writes a value under a key opened with set-value access. The type determines how the data bytes are interpreted, and the size is given in bytes. The value is created if it does not exist and overwritten if it does. Creating the key and writing a value are separate operations.
apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegSetValueExW(HKEY hKey, LPCWSTR lpValueName, DWORD Reserved, DWORD dwType, const BYTE *lpData, DWORD cbData);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open key with KEY_SET_VALUE access, or a predefined root key where permitted. The handle must have been opened or created with the necessary access.

parameters.name: lpValueName
parameters.description: The name of the value to set. A NULL pointer or an empty string sets the key's default (unnamed) value.

parameters.name: Reserved
parameters.description: Reserved. It must be zero.

parameters.name: dwType
parameters.description: The type of the data, such as REG_SZ for a null-terminated string, REG_EXPAND_SZ for a string containing environment references, or REG_DWORD for a 32-bit number.

parameters.name: lpData
parameters.description: A pointer to the data to store. For string types the buffer must contain the terminating null character, and cbData must include it.

parameters.name: cbData
parameters.description: The size of the data, in bytes. For REG_SZ and REG_EXPAND_SZ this includes the terminating null character.

return.success: ERROR_SUCCESS (zero). The value has been stored.
return.failure: A nonzero Win32 error code, returned directly. Do not call GetLastError to diagnose this function.

apis.unicode_notes: RegSetValueExW is the Unicode variant; REG_SZ and REG_EXPAND_SZ data are supplied as UTF-16LE strings. RegSetValueExA is the ANSI variant, and the encoding-neutral RegSetValueEx alias resolves at compile time.
apis.remarks: For string types, cbData must include the terminating null character. Writing a value requires KEY_SET_VALUE access on the key handle; creating the key and writing the value are separate operations.
apis.maldev_notes: Registry writes are used by installers, application settings, and system configuration. Analysts usually examine the key path and value content together, since writes alone are pervasive and often legitimate.
apis.defensive_notes: Registry value-set telemetry is a common source for detecting configuration changes. The writing process, key path, value type, and data help distinguish routine settings from unexpected modification of security-relevant keys.
apis.source_notes: Prototype, byte-count rules, and access requirement checked against Microsoft Learn (winreg.h).

apis.name: RegEnumKeyExW
apis.summary: Enumerates the subkeys of an open registry key, one call per subkey.
apis.description: RegEnumKeyExW retrieves the name and optional class and last-write time of the subkey at a given index. Callers start at index zero and increment until the function returns ERROR_NO_MORE_ITEMS. Because subkeys are not ordered, the sequence is not guaranteed to be stable, especially if the key changes during enumeration.
apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegEnumKeyExW(HKEY hKey, DWORD dwIndex, LPWSTR lpName, LPDWORD lpcchName, LPDWORD lpReserved, LPWSTR lpClass, LPDWORD lpcchClass, PFILETIME lpftLastWriteTime);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open key with KEY_ENUMERATE_SUB_KEYS access, or a predefined root key. KEY_READ includes the rights needed for ordinary enumeration.

parameters.name: dwIndex
parameters.description: The zero-based index of the subkey to retrieve. Increment it after each successful call.

parameters.name: lpName
parameters.description: A buffer that receives the subkey name, including the terminating null character. Only the name is copied, not the full key hierarchy.

parameters.name: lpcchName
parameters.description: On input, the size of lpName in characters, including space for the null terminator. On success, receives the number of characters stored, excluding the null terminator.

parameters.name: lpReserved
parameters.description: Reserved. It must be NULL.

parameters.name: lpClass
parameters.description: An optional buffer that receives the user-defined class of the enumerated subkey. NULL is permitted.

parameters.name: lpcchClass
parameters.description: An optional pointer to the size of lpClass in characters. It can be NULL only when lpClass is NULL.

parameters.name: lpftLastWriteTime
parameters.description: An optional pointer that receives the time the enumerated subkey was last written.

return.success: ERROR_SUCCESS (zero) for each subkey retrieved.
return.failure: A nonzero Win32 error code, returned directly. ERROR_NO_MORE_ITEMS ends a successful enumeration; ERROR_MORE_DATA means lpName was too small.

apis.unicode_notes: RegEnumKeyExW is the Unicode variant and expresses buffer sizes in characters. RegEnumKeyExA is the ANSI variant, and the encoding-neutral RegEnumKeyEx alias resolves at compile time.
apis.remarks: The buffer size is expressed in characters and must include space for the terminating null. ERROR_MORE_DATA indicates that the name did not fit; retry with a larger buffer rather than skipping the index. Do not modify the key being enumerated while the enumeration is in progress.
apis.maldev_notes: Subkey enumeration supports inventory and discovery logic in installers, management tools, and other software. Analysts may consider it alongside the key being enumerated and what the program does with the resulting names.
apis.defensive_notes: Enumeration produces multiple closely spaced registry access events. Baselining the keys a process normally enumerates is usually more informative than treating enumeration as suspicious on its own.

apis.name: RegCloseKey
apis.summary: Closes a handle to a registry key.
apis.description: RegCloseKey releases a handle returned by RegOpenKeyExW, RegCreateKeyExW, or another registry function that returns an HKEY. Closing the last handle to a key does not delete the key or any of its values. The function is the required cleanup step for key handles that are no longer needed.
apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegCloseKey(HKEY hKey);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open registry key that is to be closed. It must have been returned by a function that creates or opens a key.

return.success: ERROR_SUCCESS (zero); the handle has been closed.
return.failure: A nonzero Win32 error code, returned directly. Do not call GetLastError to diagnose this function.

apis.remarks: Registry functions return error codes directly rather than through GetLastError. Closing a key handle does not delete the key. Ensure that each handle opened by the process is closed exactly once, including on error paths.
apis.maldev_notes: Handle cleanup is ordinary resource management. In analysis, handle lifetime can help bound when a registry operation sequence ended.
apis.defensive_notes: Registry handle closure is rarely telemetered directly; key access and value events are generally more useful for building a timeline.
apis.source_notes: Prototype and LSTATUS return convention checked against Microsoft Learn (winreg.h).

apis.name: RegCreateKeyA
apis.summary: Creates the specified registry key.
apis.description: Creates the specified registry key. If the key already exists in the registry, the function opens it. Note This function is provided only for compatibility with 16-bit versions of Windows. Applications should use the RegCreateKeyEx function. However, applications that back up or restore system state including system files and registry hives should use the Volume Shadow Copy Service instead of the registry functions.
apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegCreateKeyA(HKEY hKey, LPCSTR lpSubKey, PHKEY phkResult);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open registry key. The calling process must have KEY_CREATE_SUB_KEY access to the key. For more information, see Registry Key Security and Access Rights. Access for key creation is checked against the security descriptor of the registry key, not the access mask specified when the handle was obtained. Therefore, even if hKey was opened with a samDesired of KEY_READ, it can be used in operations that create keys if allowed by its security descriptor. This handle is returned by the RegCreateKeyEx or RegOpenKeyEx function, or it can be one of the following predefined keys: HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG HKEY_CURRENT_USER HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE HKEY_USERS

parameters.name: lpSubKey
parameters.description: The name of a key that this function opens or creates. This key must be a subkey of the key identified by the hKey parameter. For more information on key names, see Structure of the Registry. If hKey is one of the predefined keys, lpSubKey may be NULL. In that case, phkResult receives the same hKey handle passed in to the function.

parameters.name: phkResult
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a handle to the opened or created key. If the key is not one of the predefined registry keys, call the RegCloseKey function after you have finished using the handle.

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is ERROR_SUCCESS.
return.failure: If the function fails, the return value is a nonzero error code defined in Winerror.h. You can use the FormatMessage function with the FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM flag to get a generic description of the error.

apis.remarks: An application cannot create a key that is a direct child of HKEY_USERS or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE. An application can create subkeys in lower levels of the HKEY_USERS or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE trees. If your service or application impersonates different users, do not use this function with HKEY_CURRENT_USER. Instead, call the RegOpenCurrentUser function. The RegCreateKey function creates all missing keys in the specified path. An application can take advantage of this behavior to create several keys at once. For example, an application can create a subkey four levels deep at the same time as the three preceding subkeys by specifying a string of the following form for the lpSubKey parameter: subkey1\subkey2\subkey3\subkey4 Note that this behavior will result in creation of unwanted keys if an existing key in the path is spelled incorrectly. > > The winreg.h header defines RegCreateKey as an alias that automatically selects the ANSI or Unicode version of this function based on the definition of the UNICODE preprocessor constant. Mixing usage of the encoding-neutral alias with code that is not encoding-neutral can lead to mismatches that result in compilation or runtime errors. For more information, see Conventions for Function Prototypes.

apis.name: RegCreateKeyExA
apis.summary: Creates the specified registry key.
apis.description: Creates the specified registry key. If the key already exists, the function opens it. Note that key names are not case sensitive. apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegCreateKeyExA(HKEY hKey, LPCSTR lpSubKey, DWORD Reserved, LPSTR lpClass, DWORD dwOptions, REGSAM samDesired, CONST LPSECURITY_ATTRIBUTES lpSecurityAttributes, PHKEY phkResult, LPDWORD lpdwDisposition);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open registry key. The calling process must have KEY_CREATE_SUB_KEY access to the key. For more information, see Registry Key Security and Access Rights. Access for key creation is checked against the security descriptor of the registry key, not the access mask specified when the handle was obtained. Therefore, even if hKey was opened with a samDesired of KEY_READ, it can be used in operations that modify the registry if allowed by its security descriptor. This handle is returned by the RegCreateKeyEx or RegOpenKeyEx function, or it can be one of the following predefined keys: HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG HKEY_CURRENT_USER HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE HKEY_USERS

parameters.name: lpSubKey
parameters.description: The name of a subkey that this function opens or creates. The subkey specified must be a subkey of the key identified by the hKey parameter; it can be up to 32 levels deep in the registry tree. For more information on key names, see Structure of the Registry. If lpSubKey is a pointer to an empty string, phkResult receives a new handle to the key specified by hKey. This parameter cannot be NULL.

parameters.name: Reserved
parameters.description: This parameter is reserved and must be zero.

parameters.name: lpClass
parameters.description: The user-defined class type of this key. This parameter may be ignored. This parameter can be NULL.

parameters.name: dwOptions
parameters.description: This parameter can be one of the following values. Value Meaning REG_OPTION_BACKUP_RESTORE 0x00000004L If this flag is set, the function ignores the samDesired parameter and attempts to open the key with the access required to backup or restore the key. If the calling thread has the SE_BACKUP_NAME privilege enabled, the key is opened with the ACCESS_SYSTEM_SECURITY and KEY_READ access rights. If the calling thread has the SE_RESTORE_NAME privilege enabled, beginning with Windows Vista, the key is opened with the ACCESS_SYSTEM_SECURITY, DELETE and KEY_WRITE access rights. If both privileges are enabled, the key has the combined access rights for both privileges. For more information, see Running with Special Privileges. REG_OPTION_CREATE_LINK 0x00000002L Note Registry symbolic links should only be used for application compatibility when absolutely necessary. This key is a symbolic link. T

parameters.name: samDesired
parameters.description: A mask that specifies the access rights for the key to be created. For more information, see Registry Key Security and Access Rights.

parameters.name: lpSecurityAttributes
parameters.description: A pointer to a SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES structure that determines whether the returned handle can be inherited by child processes. If lpSecurityAttributes is NULL, the handle cannot be inherited. The lpSecurityDescriptor member of the structure specifies a security descriptor for the new key. If lpSecurityAttributes is NULL, the key gets a default security descriptor. The ACLs in a default security descriptor for a key are inherited from its direct parent key.

parameters.name: phkResult
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives a handle to the opened or created key. If the key is not one of the predefined registry keys, call the RegCloseKey function after you have finished using the handle.

parameters.name: lpdwDisposition
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives one of the following disposition values. Value Meaning REG_CREATED_NEW_KEY 0x00000001L The key did not exist and was created. REG_OPENED_EXISTING_KEY 0x00000002L The key existed and was simply opened without being changed. If lpdwDisposition is NULL, no disposition information is returned.

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is ERROR_SUCCESS.
return.failure: If the function fails, the return value is a nonzero error code defined in Winerror.h. You can use the FormatMessage function with the FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM flag to get a generic description of the error.

apis.remarks: The key that the RegCreateKeyEx function creates has no values. An application can use the RegSetValueEx function to set key values. The RegCreateKeyEx function creates all missing keys in the specified path. An application can take advantage of this behavior to create several keys at once. apis.remarks: Calling RegFlushKey is an expensive operation that significantly affects system-wide performance as it consumes disk bandwidth and blocks modifications to all keys by all processes in the registry hive that is being flushed until the flush operation completes. RegFlushKey should only be called explicitly when an application must guarantee that registry changes are persisted to disk immediately after modification. All modifications made to keys are visible to other processes without the need to flush them to disk. Alternatively, the registry has a 'lazy flush' mechanism that flushes registry modifications to disk at regular intervals of time. In addition to this regular flush operation, registry changes are also flushed to disk at system shutdown. Allowing the 'lazy flush' to flush registry changes is the most efficient way to manage registry writes to the registry store on disk. The RegFlushKey function returns only when all the data for the hive that contains the specified key has been written to the registry store on disk. The RegFlushKey function writes out the data for other keys in the hive that have been modified since the last lazy flush or system start. After RegFlushKey returns, use RegCloseKey to close the handle to the registry key.

parameters.name: hToken
parameters.description: A handle to a primary or impersonation access token that identifies the user of interest. This can be a token handle returned by a call to LogonUser, CreateRestrictedToken, DuplicateToken, DuplicateTokenEx, OpenProcessToken, or OpenThreadToken functions. The handle must have TOKEN_QUERY access. For more information, see Access Rights for Access-Token Objects.

parameters.name: dwOptions

parameters.name: samDesired
parameters.description: A mask that specifies the desired access rights to the key. The function fails if the security descriptor of the key does not permit the requested access for the calling process. For more information, see Registry Key Security and Access Rights.

apis.remarks: The RegOpenUserClassesRoot function enables you to retrieve the merged HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT information for users other than the interactive user. For example, the server component of a client/server application could use RegOpenUserClassesRoot to retrieve the merged information for a client. RegOpenUserClassesRoot fails if the user profile for the specified user is not loaded. When a user logs on interactively, the system automatically loads the user's profile. For other users, you can call the LoadUserProfile function to load the user's profile. However, LoadUserProfile can be very time-consuming, so do not call it for this purpose unless it is absolutely necessary to have the user's merged HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT information. Applications running in the security context of the interactively logged-on user do not need to use RegOpenUserClassesRoot. These applications can call the RegOpenKeyEx function to retrieve a merged view of the HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT key for the interactive user.

apis.name: RegOverridePredefKey
apis.summary: Maps a predefined registry key to the specified registry key.
apis.description: Maps a predefined registry key to the specified registry key.
apis.prototype: LSTATUS RegOverridePredefKey(HKEY hKey, HKEY hNewHKey);

parameters.name: hKey
parameters.description: A handle to one of the following predefined keys: - HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT - HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG - HKEY_CURRENT_USER - HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE - HKEY_PERFORMANCE_DATA - HKEY_USERS

parameters.name: hNewHKey
parameters.description: A handle to an open registry key. This handle is returned by the RegCreateKeyEx or RegOpenKeyEx function. It cannot be one of the predefined keys. The function maps hKey to refer to the hNewHKey key. This affects only the calling process. If hNewHKey is NULL, the function restores the default mapping of the predefined key.

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is ERROR_SUCCESS.
return.failure: If the function fails, the return value is a nonzero error code defined in Winerror.h. You can use the FormatMessage function with the FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM flag to get a generic description of the error.

apis.remarks: The RegOverridePredefKey function is intended for software installation programs. It allows them to remap a predefined key, load a DLL component that will be installed on the system, call an entry point in the DLL, and examine the changes to the registry that the component attempted to make. The installation program can then write those changes to the locations intended by the DLL, or make changes to the data before writing it. For example, consider an installation program that installs an ActiveX control as part of an application installation. The installation program needs to call the control's DllRegisterServer entry point to enable the control to register itself. Before this call, the installation program can call RegOverridePredefKey to remap HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT to a temporary key such as HKEY_CURRENT_USER\TemporaryInstall\DllRegistration. It then calls DllRegisterServer, which causes the ActiveX control to write its registry entries to the temporary key. The installation program then calls RegOverridePredefKey again to restore the original mapping of HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT. The installation program can modify the keys written to the temporary key, if necessary, before copying them to the original HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT. After the call to RegOverridePredefKey, you can safely call RegCloseKey to close the hNewHKey handle. The system maintains its own reference to hNewHKey.
